extraction.name: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
extraction.description: One core capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) is to follow natural language instructions. However, the evaluation of such abilities is not standardized: Human evaluations are expensive, slow, and not objectively reproducible, while LLM-based auto-evaluation is potentially biased or limited by the ability of the evaluator LLM. To overcome these issues, we introduce Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval) for large language models. IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark. It focuses on a set of “verifiable instructions” such as “write in more than 400 words” and “mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times”. We identified 25 types of those verifiable instructions and constructed around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions. We show evaluation results of two widely available LLMs on the market.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We identified 25 types of verifiable instructions and constructed around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions. Altogether, we create a list of 25 verifiable instructions. We further create a set of 541 prompts, with each prompt containing one or multiple verifiable instructions. Prompts were created through four steps: First, a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt was generated. Then, few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical prompts. As the third step, another few-shot prompting based approach was applied to rephrase each prompt to increase the diversity of phrasing. Finally, the rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited one by one.

extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses 'verifiable instructions' which are amenable to objective verification of compliance, enabling a fully automatic and accurate assessment of a machine model’s ability to follow directions. The verification is performed by a simple, interpretable, and deterministic program.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Even though instructions can be verified using simple heuristics and programming, false negatives can occur. To alleviate this, a 'loose accuracy score' of instruction following is computed. This involves transforming each response using eight transformation functions: 1. Removing commonly seen font modifiers in markdown syntax (e.g., '*' and '**'). 2. Removing the first line of the response (e.g., intros like 'Sure, here it is:'). 3. Removing the last line of the response (e.g., outros like 'Hope it helps.'). Combinations of these transformations are also applied. While this reduces false negatives, it may introduce false positives, so it is considered a complement to the original strict criterion.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: As part of future work, there are plans to improve the prompts and verifiable instructions to make them more related to real-world applications. The approach will also be expanded with more verifiable instructions and support for multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial for the precision, safety, and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems. Ensuring LLMs consistently adhere to given directives is paramount.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current implementation of IFEval can be improved across many fronts. While the focus is on verifiable instructions, very few instructions are 100% objectively and automatically verifiable, with edge cases where it's hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The loose instruction-following verification process, while reducing false negatives, is likely to introduce false positives. Specific areas for improvement include increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and extending to multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: IFEval is a benchmark to evaluate the instruction following ability of LLMs using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions. It is designed for training, testing, and validation of LLMs. Researchers can use evaluation results to draw insights on what types of instructions are not usually followed and compare different large language models on various instruction types.
